subtitle: Lesson 18 · Working With GPUs in PyTorch

eyebrow: Pick a device once, use it everywhere
code:
import torch

device = torch.device("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")
print(device)   # cuda or cpu
caption: Degrades gracefully to CPU instead of crashing when no GPU is visible

eyebrow: Model and inputs must share a device
code:
model = model.to(device)

for inputs, labels in dataloader:
    inputs = inputs.to(device)
    labels = labels.to(device)
    outputs = model(inputs)
caption: A tensor's .to() returns a new tensor — reassignment is required, not optional

eyebrow: Two ways to move a tensor

steps.label: .to(device)
steps.sub: same code path for cpu, cuda, or mps

code:
>>> output = model(cpu_tensor)
RuntimeError: Expected all tensors to be on the same
device, but found at least two devices, cuda:0 and cpu!
caption: Usually one fresh tensor created without device= and never moved

subtitle: Once tensors are on the right device, how fast they got there starts to matter.
